youtube.title: Why GTA 6 reportedly runs at 30 fps on consoles
youtube.description: If you were counting on a 60 fps mode in GTA 6 on day one, Rockstar hasn't promised you one. Rockstar North's Rob Nelson reportedly told YouTuber Davy Jones that consoles currently run the game at 30 fps and that he would need to ask the technical team about a 60 fps option. GTA 5 only got 60 fps on PS5 and Xbox Series consoles, and Red Dead Redemption 2 still has no official 60 fps upgrade. Sources: Kotaku, Tom's Hardware, Flow Games.
title_variants: GTA 6 is reportedly 30 fps on console, with no 60 promised
Rockstar hasn't promised 60 fps in GTA 6, per reports

claims.claim: Rob Nelson, head of development at Rockstar North, reportedly told YouTuber Davy Jones that GTA 6 currently runs at 30 fps on console during development.
Nelson said it is still necessary to consult the technical team to determine whether there will be a 60 fps option at launch or later.
Tom's Hardware quotes Nelson as needing to "consult the technical team" about 60 fps at launch or later, as relayed on Jones's Flow Games podcast.
GTA 5 did not get a 60 fps option until the upgrade for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.
GTA 5 ran at 30 fps on PS3 and PS4 before getting 60 fps on PS5, two console generations after its original release.
Red Dead Redemption 2 still does not have an official 60 fps upgrade for modern consoles.

issues.quote: Why GTA 6 reportedly runs at 30 fps on consoles
issues.problem: The title promises an explanation of why, but the script gives no reason for the 30 fps cap. Tom's Hardware carries a Digital Foundry theory about CPU load, which the script does not use. This is a packaging mismatch, not an unsupported fact.

issues.quote: GTA 5 only got 60 on PS5, two generations later.
issues.problem: The spoken line leaves out Xbox Series X/S, which Kotaku says got the 60 fps upgrade as well. The description states it correctly. "Two generations later" is consistent with Tom's Hardware's PS3/PS4 to PS5 history.

check.summary: The script passes with no blockers; every factual claim is supported by Kotaku and Tom's Hardware. Nelson's 30 fps comment is hedged with "reportedly", and the "consult the technical team" quote is correctly attributed via Flow Games. The GTA 5 and Red Dead 2 history matches the sources. The "years, not weeks" line and the advice to plan around 30 are flagged as unconfirmed or framed as opinion. The two minor issues are a title that promises a "why" the script does not deliver and the spoken omission of Xbox Series.
